rv.q: I can offer this production no higher praise than to say, now I get it.
City Lit distinguishes itself in the selection of this play, and in an absolutely wonderful production.
This latest production by City Lit is profound and penetrating.

It’s the mood captured by director Terry McCabe’s perfectly cast, skillfully paced staging of “Birthday Party,” which brings to the fore both the play’s comically overdone domestic pseudo-normality and its sense of a mounting threat that’s palpable without being definable.
The interrogation of Stanley under the guise of having fun is creepy, and this party in his honor thus becomes a means of deliberately toying with his emotions.

cn.t: CityLit's gripping production of Pinter's "The Birthday Party" earns strong praise for its flawless performances and masterful navigation of the play's shift from low-key humor to sinister psychological menace.
